1.explanation:
1. src/js/components/Calendar/StyledCalendar.js – this file defines the core flex and sliding styles (e.g. display: flex on each week, keyframe animations for sliding). IE11 needs proper vendor-prefixed properties (for example, it doesn’t recognize the custom “flex-justify” shorthand nor unprefixed keyframes), so the weeks collapse into a single column. 
2. src/js/components/Calendar/Calendar.js – this is the Calendar component wiring together the styled elements. It calculates the weeks and renders them into StyledWeek containers. Any fix to the markup or to how the StyledWeeks/StyledWeek wrappers are applied needs to happen here so that the corrected CSS (for IE11) is actually used. 
3. webpack.config.babel.js – the build pipeline is responsible for running Babel and styled-components through PostCSS/autoprefixer. To support IE11 flexbox and keyframes, the Webpack configuration must include PostCSS with an IE11 target and necessary vendor prefixes. Adjusting this file ensures that the CSS injected by styled-components is transpiled and prefixed correctly for IE11.
1.bug_scenario: In IE11, the Grommet2 Calendar popup renders all of the day cells stacked in a single column instead of in a multi-column grid. In the provided screenshot you can see the days “8”, “15”, “22”, “30” all piled up one on top of the other under “July 2018”. This indicates that the flex layout or animation CSS isn’t being applied correctly in IE11, so the weeks aren’t laid out side by side.
